body: /cc @kchodorow this looks related to external repositories. I feel like I have already seen that but I cannot remember how.

Can you share what your WORKSPACE file looks like?  

The reason it's got /home/tcj/src instead of /home/tcj/src/blaze_workspace is due to some hackery shoehorning //external into being a package.  Generally, the package defined by foo/bar/BUILD finds its source root by stripping the two pieces of package name (foo/bar) off of the full directory path (/home/tcj/src/blaze_workspace/foo/bar becomes /home/tcj/src/blaze_workspace).  However, for the external package, its name "package name" is "external" and it's already rooted at /home/tcj/src/blaze_workspace, so Bazel assumes there is one path piece to strip off and removes the blaze_workspace.

Sure no problem. It's pretty tame - just a bunch of maven_jars and the Android SDK setup

[Here it is](http://pastebin.com/MZbbbjf0)

[Here's](http://pastebin.com/u4T086aH) my BUILD file in question, trying to build :googleplay

Perhaps the duplication comes from having multiple //external:android deps?

`
package(
  default_visibility = ["//visibility:public"],
)

genrule(
  name = "manifest",
  srcs = ["//java/com/jeffreys/euchre:manifest_template"],
  outs = ["AndroidManifest.xml"],
  cmd = "$(location //java/com/jeffreys/soyrenderer) $(location //java/com/jeffreys/euchre:manifest_template) com.jeffreys.euchre.manifest package com.jeffreys.euchre application com.jeffreys.common.euchre.common.GooglePlayFreeApplication > \"$@\"",
  tools = ["//java/com/jeffreys/soyrenderer"],
)

android_binary(
  name = "googleplay_proguard",
  manifest = ":manifest",
  proguard_specs = ["//java/com/jeffreys/euchre:proguard"],
  proguard_generate_mapping = 1,
  resource_files = ["//java/com/jeffreys/euchre:resources"],
  deps = [
    "//java/com/jeffreys/common/euchre/android",
    "//external:android/appcompat_v4",
    "//external:android/mediarouter_v7",
    "//external:android/palette_v7",
  ],
)

android_binary(
  name = "googleplay",
  manifest = ":manifest",
  resource_files = ["//java/com/jeffreys/euchre:resources"],
  deps = [
    "//java/com/jeffreys/common/euchre/android",
    "//external:android/appcompat_v4",
    "//external:android/mediarouter_v7",
    "//external:android/palette_v7",
  ],
)
`
I've been trying to reproduce it (and found another bug), but haven't been able to, yet.  Do you have a simpler case that reproduces the issue?

This rule crashes it immediately:

android_library(
  name = "test",
  deps = [
    "//external:android/mediarouter_v7",
    "//external:android/palette_v7",
  ],
)

Basically anything with multiple "//external" will cause the error.
No, I just found the AST bug while trying to reproduce this.
And reproduced (finally).  A less invasive workaround is using `@repo//path/to/your:target` syntax instead of `//external:whatever`.

I'm going to decrease the priority of this to P2 since there is a viable workaround, but here's what I've found debugging:

Two different Package(external)s are added to the configured target's transitive packages.  One is added by resolveConfiguredTargetDependencies() and the other is added by resolveAspectDependencies, so I'm guessing that something about the aspect dependencies is not resolving //external right.
